newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - White gets another shot at test team.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - White gets another shot at test team.

text.p: PALMERSTON North, Jan 13 - England cricket allrounder Craig White is developing a well-stamped passport.
In the last 18 months, he has become an international wanderer on behalf of the England side, NZPA reports.
The 27-year-old joined the England squad on Sunday morning, making New Zealand the fourth country in which he has played cricket in the last four months.
White was touring Australia with the England A team before Christmas when he was called across to Zimbabwe to act as cover for injured Ronnie Irani.
He played one test and two one-dayers before returning to Australia for a few days break with his family before arriving in New Zealand.
Late in 1996 he was in Pakistan with England A, flew to South Africa for the senior team's one-day programme then on to the World Cup in India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
An aggressive fast-medium bowler, athletic fielder and capable lower middle order batsman, White's England career comprises seven tests and 12 one-dayers.
White made his test debut against New Zealand in 1994, having taken seven wickets and hit a half century in Yorkshire's innings win over the tourists just beforehand.
He made 51 on debut at Lord's, the test best remembered for Dion Nash's feat of taking 11 wickets and hitting a half century for New Zealand.
But White strained side muscles on the Ashes tour of Australia in 1994-95, then had another injury to the same part of his body during last year's World Cup.
Now he's hoping to make the most of another opportunity to reclaim a test spot.
"It's happened to me in the past couple of years with injuries. They call for me and it's another way back in," the Yorkshire-born, Australian-raised White said.
He admitted his test and one-day records don't yet warrant bright lights -- 166 runs at 15.09 and nine wickets at 41.66 in tests, 117 runs at 11.7 and nine wickets at 38.11 in one-dayers.
"I haven't had a good record when I've come in. That was due to injuries. When I started to do well I got injuries.
"I'd just like to have a go free from injury and see how I go," he added.

White, who spent time at the Australian Cricket Academy in his teenage years and made a tour of New Zealand with them, showed yesterday he has a sharp turn of pace, rapping team mate John Crawley's fingers with a flier during practice.
England coach David Lloyd is hoping White's time has come.
"He had an excellent tour to Australia (before Christmas). He could have shrunk there with his (Australian) background, but he responded very well.
"He needs confidence in his own game and the opportunity is here to come through and cement a place," he said.
